svg.text: A plain-language map of how Claude Code talks to your notch

g.title: Claude Code: The tool you already use. At key moments it rings a hook.
Helper: A tiny program Claude Code starts for every event. Passes it on, waits, prints your answer back.
Private Socket: A private pipe on your Mac. Nobody else can open it.
NotchGate App: Logs the event, reads your switches, picks: card, auto-allow, or leave to the terminal.
Your Switches: Every on/off lives in app.notchgate.NotchGate.plist and is saved the moment you flip it.
Claude Hook List: Where NotchGate tells Claude Code to call the helper. Backed up before every change.
Status Files: Plan limits, model, context and cost, saved by the helper from Claude's status line.
Live Activity: In memory only: what each session is doing, tool counts, to-dos, file changes.
Waiting List: Requests that need you wait in this queue. If you answer in the terminal first, the card disappears.
Risk Check: With auto-allow on, risky commands (rm -rf, sudo, git push --force…) still ask you.
Your Notch: A card grows out of the notch. Hover it to see every Claude session.
You: Click Allow / Deny, pick an answer, or type the next prompt.
Prompt Typer: Types your prompt into the right terminal and presses Return.
Your Terminal: tmux, iTerm2, Terminal.app, Cursor / VS Code (via helper extension), WezTerm.
GitHub: The only internet call. Checks for a newer NotchGate every 6 hours.
